svg.title: HTTP unique-event and aggregate-delivered-frame throughput
svg.desc: Two zero-baseline panels at the recorded reader counts. Blue circles are raw; orange diamonds are runtime. Each dot is a run rate; lines are medians and whiskers are min-max. Aggregate delivery multiplies events by reader count, so its increase does not imply greater producer speed.

rect.style: stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: HTTP throughput: unique events and delivered frames
64 events/run | 128 ASCII message bytes (+ metadata) | SQLite WAL / NORMAL | 1 producer | localhost HTTP

circle.style: stroke: rgb(0%,44%,69%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

path.style: stroke: rgb(83%,36%,0%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 2.5; stroke-dasharray: 7, 4;

polygon.style: stroke: rgb(83%,36%,0%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: Dots: 3 runs | line: median | whiskers: min-max (not CI)
Recorded 2026-10-18 | Apple M3 Pro | Python 3.11.10 | SQLite 3.54.0
Source: baseline-2026-10-18.json | input SHA256 and values: series.json

g.text: Delivered business frames = unique events x readers. Larger fanout does not mean a faster producer.
Both rates use earliest request start to latest reader completion; terminal frames are excluded from counts.
